title: TestPilot Quantitative Evaluation Question Matrix
description: Comprehensive 30-question quantitative evaluation matrix defining empirical metrics, mathematical formulas, required data schemas, aggregation policies, and answerability criteria for benchmarking change-aware regression test selection across heterogeneous repositories.

question_categories.name: Category A — Test Selection Quality
question_categories.description: Precision, recall, F1 score, test reduction, and baseline comparisons against independently validated relevant-test ground truth.

question_categories.name: Category B — Dependency and Impact Analysis
question_categories.description: Accuracy of AST changed-symbol detection, direct-caller extraction, transitive call propagation, semantic classification, and evidence citations.

question_categories.name: Category C — Repository RAG and Evidence Retrieval
question_categories.description: Retrieval precision/recall@K, Sourcegraph vs local fallback trade-offs, RAG test-selection ablation deltas, unsupported claim rates, and resilience.

question_categories.name: Category D — Test Generation and Ground Truth
question_categories.description: Candidate test execution viability, mutation detection sensitivity (fault detection), historical bug reproduction, and human review throughput.

question_categories.name: Category E — Performance and Scalability
question_categories.description: Wall-clock runtime, time savings over full regression, pipeline stage latency overhead, and computational resource scaling.

question_categories.name: Category F — Reliability and Generalization
question_categories.description: Deterministic run-to-run consistency, cross-repository performance variation, and robustness across change types and language ecosystems.

question_categories.name: Category G — Evaluation Validity and Usability
question_categories.description: Scientific benchmark auditability, revision reproducibility, provenance completeness, and automated evaluation completion rates.

evaluation_configurations.name: Full Regression
evaluation_configurations.description: Executes 100% of discovered tests in the eligible test universe. Yields upper bound on recall (100%) and lower bound on reduction (0%).

evaluation_configurations.name: Naive Baseline
evaluation_configurations.description: Heuristic token/filename matching (e.g. test_<symbol>.py). Emulates standard keyword-based CI selection.

evaluation_configurations.name: TestPilot
evaluation_configurations.description: AST-qualified symbol identity, call graph traversal, and deterministic boundary analysis without external vector RAG.

evaluation_configurations.name: TestPilot + Repository RAG
evaluation_configurations.description: Combines deterministic AST boundary analysis with repository-isolated vector embedding retrieval for semantic context.

aggregation_policy.zero_denominator_handling: Explicit null (displays as N/A in UI), never fabricated or treated as 0.0 or 1.0.
aggregation_policy.missing_ground_truth_policy: Excluded from aggregate scoring; missing ground truth is never penalized as a zero score.
aggregation_policy.ground_truth_independence: Ground truth caller sets must be verified independently of TestPilot prediction models.
aggregation_policy.micro_averaging: Sum raw TP, FP, FN counts across all eligible runs before computing overall precision, recall, and F1.
aggregation_policy.macro_averaging: Calculate per-repository metric rates first, then report their unweighted arithmetic mean.
aggregation_policy.fault_detection_separation: Mutant kill rate and fault-detection metrics are strictly separated from test selection precision and recall.

questions.category: Category A — Test Selection Quality
questions.question: What is the test-selection precision of each evaluation configuration against independently validated relevant-test ground truth?
questions.objective: Quantify the proportion of selected tests that are genuinely relevant to modified code, assessing resistance to false-positive test executions.

metrics.name: Precision
metrics.definition: Ratio of true positive selected tests to total selected tests.
metrics.formula: TP / (TP + FP) if (TP + FP) > 0 else null

questions.methodology: For each evaluated benchmark case, compare predicted test identifiers against verified ground truth test callers. Compute TP as the intersection and FP as predicted tests outside ground truth.
questions.formula: TP / (TP + FP) if (TP + FP) > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Side-by-side comparison across full_regression, naive_baseline, testpilot, and testpilot_rag.
questions.aggregation: Micro: sum(TP) / (sum(TP) + sum(FP)); Macro: average of per-repository precisions.
questions.interpretation: Higher precision indicates fewer wasted test executions. A value of null indicates no tests were selected.
questions.limitations: Incomplete ground truth in real-world repositories can artificially penalize precision if relevant callers were omitted from ground truth.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires benchmark cases with verified ground_truth.is_verified == true and at least one configuration selecting >= 1 test.

questions.category: Category A — Test Selection Quality
questions.question: What is the test-selection recall of each evaluation configuration against independently validated relevant-test ground truth?
questions.objective: Measure the completeness of regression test selection in identifying all tests required to exercise changed behaviors.

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.definition: Ratio of true positive selected tests to total ground truth relevant tests.
metrics.formula: TP / (TP + FN) if (TP + FN) > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Intersect predicted tests with verified ground truth callers (TP). Compute FN as ground truth tests omitted from the selection.
questions.formula: TP / (TP + FN) if (TP + FN) > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Benchmark Full Regression (100% recall upper bound) against Naive Baseline, TestPilot, and TestPilot + Repository RAG.
questions.aggregation: Micro: sum(TP) / (sum(TP) + sum(FN)); Macro: average of per-repository recalls.
questions.interpretation: High recall ensures regression safety. Values below 100% represent missed regression risks.
questions.limitations: Recall can only be computed when ground truth contains at least one verified test caller (|GT| > 0).
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires benchmark cases with verified ground truth caller sets containing >= 1 test.

questions.category: Category A — Test Selection Quality
questions.question: What is the F1 score achieved by each evaluation configuration across evaluated benchmark cases?
questions.objective: Assess the balanced trade-off between precision (minimizing false positives) and recall (minimizing missed regressions).

metrics.name: F1 Score
metrics.definition: Harmonic mean of precision and recall.
metrics.formula: 2 * (Precision * Recall) / (Precision + Recall) if (Precision + Recall) > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Compute precision and recall from verified counts, then take their harmonic mean. Return null if both precision and recall are zero or undefined.
questions.formula: 2 * (Precision * Recall) / (Precision + Recall) if (Precision + Recall) > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Evaluate across all 4 configurations to identify the optimal balance point.
questions.aggregation: Micro: computed from micro precision and micro recall; Macro: average of per-repository F1 scores.
questions.interpretation: F1 balances precision and recall; prevents strategies that maximize one at the catastrophic expense of the other from appearing superior.
questions.limitations: Weights precision and recall equally, whereas safety-critical CI may prioritize recall over precision.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires both precision and recall to be computable on valid ground truth.

questions.category: Category A — Test Selection Quality
questions.question: What percentage test reduction is achieved relative to the eligible test universe for each configuration?
questions.objective: Quantify the reduction in test executions achieved by selection strategies compared to running the entire test suite.

metrics.name: Test Reduction Percentage
metrics.definition: Percentage of tests in the eligible test universe omitted from execution.
metrics.formula: (Total_Tests - Selected_Tests) / Total_Tests * 100 if Total_Tests > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Count discovered eligible tests across repository test suites. Subtract the count of selected tests, divide by total tests, and multiply by 100.
questions.formula: (Total_Tests - Selected_Tests) / Total_Tests * 100 if Total_Tests > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Full Regression achieves 0% reduction by definition. Compare TestPilot, Naive Baseline, and TestPilot + Repository RAG.
questions.aggregation: Micro: (sum(Total_Tests) - sum(Selected_Tests)) / sum(Total_Tests) * 100; Macro: mean of per-repo reduction rates.
questions.interpretation: Higher reduction indicates greater CI compute efficiency, provided recall remains high.
questions.limitations: High reduction is meaningless or harmful if essential tests are missed (low recall).
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires non-empty test discovery (Total_Tests > 0).

questions.category: Category A — Test Selection Quality
questions.question: How does TestPilot compare directly against the Naive Baseline in selection quality and runtime?
questions.objective: Determine whether AST-qualified symbol identity provides statistically significant precision gains over simple token/name matching without sacrificing recall or incurring excessive runtime latency.

metrics.name: Precision Delta
metrics.definition: Absolute difference in precision between TestPilot and Naive Baseline.
metrics.formula: Precision_TestPilot - Precision_Naive

metrics.name: Recall Delta
metrics.definition: Absolute difference in recall between TestPilot and Naive Baseline.
metrics.formula: Recall_TestPilot - Recall_Naive

metrics.name: Latency Ratio
metrics.definition: Ratio of TestPilot selection runtime to Naive Baseline runtime.
metrics.formula: Latency_TestPilot / Latency_Naive if Latency_Naive > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Execute both TestPilot and Naive Baseline on identical benchmark cases with pinned revisions. Compute differences in precision, recall, F1, and wall-clock execution time.
questions.formula: Precision_TestPilot - Precision_Naive
questions.comparison: Direct paired difference: TestPilot vs Naive Baseline.
questions.aggregation: Paired difference of aggregate micro and macro metrics across repositories.
questions.interpretation: Positive precision delta demonstrates elimination of name collision false positives. Negative recall delta indicates potential recall loss on dynamic dispatch.
questions.limitations: Heuristic token matching performance varies dramatically based on repository naming conventions.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires both configurations to be evaluated on the same benchmark cases.

questions.category: Category A — Test Selection Quality
questions.question: What is the change in selection quality and runtime when Repository RAG is enabled?
questions.objective: Quantify the marginal benefit and runtime overhead of semantic vector retrieval over deterministic AST selection alone.

metrics.name: RAG Recall Improvement
metrics.definition: Gain in recall when augmenting TestPilot with Repository RAG.
metrics.formula: Recall_TestPilot_RAG - Recall_TestPilot

metrics.name: RAG Runtime Overhead
metrics.definition: Additional latency incurred by embedding query and vector store search.
metrics.formula: Latency_TestPilot_RAG - Latency_TestPilot

questions.methodology: Run paired benchmark evaluations with RAG disabled vs RAG enabled with ChromaDB and Ollama embeddings on identical revisions.
questions.formula: Recall_TestPilot_RAG - Recall_TestPilot
questions.comparison: TestPilot + Repository RAG vs Core TestPilot.
questions.aggregation: Mean delta across all benchmark runs with active vector stores.
questions.interpretation: Positive recall delta indicates successful recovery of non-explicitly referenced tests. Large positive latency indicates vector indexing overhead.
questions.limitations: Requires indexed vector stores and active embedding models for each subject repository.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires execution of the TestPilot + Repository RAG configuration with verified vector index.

questions.category: Category B — Dependency and Impact Analysis
questions.question: What are the precision and recall of changed-symbol detection across modified Git revisions?
questions.objective: Evaluate how accurately the repository evolution engine extracts modified functions, methods, and classes from raw Git diffs.

metrics.name: Symbol Detection Precision
metrics.definition: Ratio of genuinely modified symbols detected to total symbols reported as changed.
metrics.formula: TP_symbols / (TP_symbols + FP_symbols) if (TP_symbols + FP_symbols) > 0 else null

metrics.name: Symbol Detection Recall
metrics.definition: Ratio of genuinely modified symbols detected to total ground truth modified symbols.
metrics.formula: TP_symbols / (TP_symbols + FN_symbols) if (TP_symbols + FN_symbols) > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Compare symbols extracted by RepositoryEvolutionEngine against manual AST diff annotations of added, modified, and deleted constructs.
questions.formula: TP_symbols / (TP_symbols + FP_symbols) if (TP_symbols + FP_symbols) > 0 else null
questions.comparison: AST diff analysis vs ground truth symbol changes.
questions.aggregation: Micro sum of symbol counts across commit pairs.
questions.interpretation: High precision avoids initiating blast radius exploration on irrelevant code; high recall ensures all modifications are tracked.
questions.limitations: Non-code changes (docstrings, comments, whitespace) must be filtered to prevent false positives.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires benchmark cases with ground_truth.expected_changed_symbols annotated.

questions.category: Category B — Dependency and Impact Analysis
questions.question: What are the precision and recall of direct-caller identification from AST call-graph extraction?
questions.objective: Measure how effectively static AST call site extraction identifies functions and methods that directly invoke changed symbols.

metrics.name: Direct Caller Precision
metrics.definition: Ratio of true callers identified to total candidate callers extracted.
metrics.formula: TP_callers / (TP_callers + FP_callers) if (TP_callers + FP_callers) > 0 else null

metrics.name: Direct Caller Recall
metrics.definition: Ratio of true callers identified to all verified callers in the codebase.
metrics.formula: TP_callers / (TP_callers + FN_callers) if (TP_callers + FN_callers) > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Traverse AST to extract Call nodes. Resolve receiver types and qualified names. Compare extracted callers with manually verified call graph edges.
questions.formula: TP_callers / (TP_callers + FP_callers) if (TP_callers + FP_callers) > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Static AST caller extraction vs verified call graph ground truth.
questions.aggregation: Micro pooled sum of caller identifications across repositories.
questions.interpretation: High precision reflects receiver disambiguation; low recall indicates unhandled dynamic calls or aliases.
questions.limitations: Dynamic dispatch, reflection (getattr), and monkey-patching cannot be fully resolved statically.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires call graph verification ground truth for target symbols.

questions.category: Category B — Dependency and Impact Analysis
questions.question: What is the accuracy of identifying transitive dependency impact through multi-hop call hierarchies?
questions.objective: Quantify the correctness of downstream impact propagation across call chains of depth >= 2.

metrics.name: Transitive Impact Accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction of multi-hop impacted symbols correctly identified without over-expansion.
metrics.formula: Correctly_Identified_Transitive / Total_Verified_Transitive if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Propagate impact across call graph edges up to max_depth=3. Check whether all ground_truth.expected_impacted_symbols are present.
questions.formula: Correctly_Identified_Transitive / Total_Verified_Transitive if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: 1-hop direct callers vs 2-hop and 3-hop transitive propagation.
questions.aggregation: Macro average accuracy grouped by call chain depth.
questions.interpretation: Assesses whether blast radius expansion captures distant regressions without exploding candidate test set sizes.
questions.limitations: Deep call graphs in large frameworks can lead to rapid blast radius explosion if unconstrained.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires benchmark cases with ground_truth.expected_impacted_symbols containing transitive targets.

questions.category: Category B — Dependency and Impact Analysis
questions.question: What is the semantic dependency classification performance against independently reviewed labels?
questions.objective: Evaluate the precision, recall, and specificity of classifying dependencies as structural, architectural, or behavioral contracts.

metrics.name: Semantic Classification Agreement
metrics.definition: Cohen's kappa or accuracy between predicted dependency types and expert-labeled dependency types.
metrics.formula: Correctly_Classified_Dependencies / Total_Evaluated_Dependencies if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Compare semantic dependency classifications produced by SemanticEvolutionEngine against expert-reviewed dependency annotations.
questions.formula: Correctly_Classified_Dependencies / Total_Evaluated_Dependencies if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Rule-based AST typing vs LLM-assisted semantic dependency classification.
questions.aggregation: Pooled accuracy across all evaluated dependency pairs.
questions.interpretation: High agreement confirms that semantic dependency classifiers accurately distinguish hard structural dependencies from soft conceptual linkages.
questions.limitations: Expert agreement on semantic dependency boundaries can be subjective without formal specifications.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires curated dataset of labeled structural vs semantic dependency pairs.

questions.category: Category B — Dependency and Impact Analysis
questions.question: What is the coverage and validity of evidence references supporting impact claims?
questions.objective: Determine the proportion of selected tests or impacted symbols that have verifiable AST call sites, diff hunks, or specification citations.

metrics.name: Evidence Validity Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of generated evidence records pointing to existing, verifiable file paths and symbol names.
metrics.formula: Valid_Evidence_Records / Total_Evidence_Records * 100 if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Inspect every TestSelectionEvidence object in evaluation runs. Verify that referenced files exist, symbols are present at stated line numbers, and callers invoke target symbols.
questions.formula: Valid_Evidence_Records / Total_Evidence_Records * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Deterministic AST evidence validity vs LLM-generated rationale validity.
questions.aggregation: Micro sum: total valid evidence items / total evidence items * 100.
questions.interpretation: Ensures explainability is grounded in code reality rather than fabricated explanations.
questions.limitations: Valid syntax and file paths do not guarantee semantic necessity of the test selection.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires evaluation runs with non-empty evidence_records lists.

questions.category: Category B — Dependency and Impact Analysis
questions.question: What is the accuracy of associations between changed symbols, affected code, and relevant tests?
questions.objective: Measure end-to-end alignment accuracy between modified source symbols, impacted business logic, and test assertions.

metrics.name: End-to-End Association Accuracy
metrics.definition: Proportion of complete change-impact-test triplets that are factually validated.
metrics.formula: Valid_Triplets / Total_Generated_Triplets * 100 if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Audit the full traceability chain: changed symbol -> intermediate caller -> selected test. Verify each link in the chain against code AST.
questions.formula: Valid_Triplets / Total_Generated_Triplets * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Direct symbol-to-test matching vs multi-step impact chain association.
questions.aggregation: Macro average association accuracy across benchmark suites.
questions.interpretation: High triplet accuracy proves that tests were selected for the right structural reason, not by coincidence.
questions.limitations: Difficult to evaluate automatically when multiple changes occur in a single commit.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires isolated single-concern commits or benchmark cases with atomic change ground truth.

questions.category: Category C — Repository RAG and Evidence Retrieval
questions.question: What is the retrieval precision@K of Repository RAG when querying for relevant tests and documentation?
questions.objective: Measure the fraction of top-K retrieved code and test chunks that are genuinely relevant to the change context.

metrics.name: Precision@K
metrics.definition: Number of relevant retrieved chunks in the top-K results divided by K.
metrics.formula: Relevant_Chunks_in_Top_K / K

questions.methodology: Query RepoVectorStore with diff summaries and changed symbol names. For K in [3, 5, 10], compute what proportion of returned chunks match ground truth relevant files and tests.
questions.formula: Relevant_Chunks_in_Top_K / K
questions.comparison: Evaluate across K=3, K=5, and K=10; compare dense embeddings against BM25/keyword retrieval.
questions.aggregation: Mean Precision@K across all benchmark queries.
questions.interpretation: High Precision@K ensures that context windows are not diluted with irrelevant code chunks.
questions.limitations: Depends heavily on chunking strategy (function-level vs line-based) and embedding model domain knowledge.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires indexed repository vector stores and annotated chunk relevance ground truth.

questions.category: Category C — Repository RAG and Evidence Retrieval
questions.question: What is the evidence recall@K of Repository RAG against ground-truth evidence requirements?
questions.objective: Determine the proportion of all necessary ground-truth supporting evidence captured within the top-K retrieved artifacts.

metrics.name: Recall@K
metrics.definition: Number of relevant chunks in top-K divided by total relevant chunks in ground truth.
metrics.formula: Relevant_Chunks_in_Top_K / Total_Ground_Truth_Relevant_Chunks if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Count how many distinct ground truth evidence items appear in the top-K retrieved results. Divide by total required ground truth evidence items.
questions.formula: Relevant_Chunks_in_Top_K / Total_Ground_Truth_Relevant_Chunks if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Measure recall progression as K increases from 1 to 20.
questions.aggregation: Macro average Recall@K across all evaluated benchmark scenarios.
questions.interpretation: Measures whether top-K retrieval is broad enough to catch all relevant tests or whether critical evidence falls outside the retrieval horizon.
questions.limitations: Large repositories with diffuse changes may require excessively large K to achieve high recall.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires complete ground truth evidence inventories for each evaluated case.

questions.category: Category C — Repository RAG and Evidence Retrieval
questions.question: How does Sourcegraph retrieval compare to local AST/repository fallback in relevance, coverage, latency, and failure rate?
questions.objective: Evaluate the empirical trade-offs between remote enterprise code intelligence and zero-dependency local AST fallback.

metrics.name: Sourcegraph vs Local Latency Delta
metrics.definition: Difference in search and reference extraction latency between Sourcegraph and LocalCodeGraphFallback.
metrics.formula: Latency_Sourcegraph - Latency_Local_AST

metrics.name: Caller Set Overlap
metrics.definition: Jaccard similarity between caller sets discovered by Sourcegraph vs LocalCodeGraphFallback.
metrics.formula: |Callers_SG ∩ Callers_Local| / |Callers_SG ∪ Callers_Local| if Union > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Execute identical symbol reference queries against live Sourcegraph OSS instance and against LocalCodeGraphFallback. Compare result sets, latency, and error rates.
questions.formula: null
questions.comparison: Sourcegraph GraphQL API vs Local Tree-sitter / AST Fallback.
questions.aggregation: Paired summary across all symbol lookups.
questions.interpretation: Determines whether enterprise indexers justify network dependency and setup cost over self-contained local AST parsing.
questions.limitations: Subject to network variability and Sourcegraph container indexing latency.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires access to both an active Sourcegraph endpoint and local repository files.

questions.category: Category C — Repository RAG and Evidence Retrieval
questions.question: What are the absolute and relative test-selection quality changes between TestPilot and TestPilot + Repository RAG?
questions.objective: Quantify whether semantic RAG retrieval recovers tests missed by static AST analysis (e.g. dynamic fixtures or config-driven tests).

metrics.name: Absolute Precision Delta
metrics.definition: Precision(TestPilot_RAG) - Precision(TestPilot)
metrics.formula: Precision_RAG - Precision_TestPilot

metrics.name: Absolute Recall Delta
metrics.definition: Recall(TestPilot_RAG) - Recall(TestPilot)
metrics.formula: Recall_RAG - Recall_TestPilot

questions.methodology: Pairwise comparison of identical benchmark cases evaluated under TestPilot vs TestPilot + Repository RAG.
questions.formula: Recall_RAG - Recall_TestPilot
questions.comparison: TestPilot + Repository RAG vs Core TestPilot.
questions.aggregation: Micro and macro deltas across repositories.
questions.interpretation: A positive recall delta with minimal precision drop demonstrates that semantic retrieval adds real coverage without generating false positives.
questions.limitations: RAG effectiveness depends heavily on prompt version, chunk boundaries, and vector database embeddings.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires benchmark runs completed under both configurations on identical pinned commits.

questions.category: Category C — Repository RAG and Evidence Retrieval
questions.question: What is the rate of evaluated semantic or RAG claims lacking sufficient supporting evidence?
questions.objective: Quantify hallucination or unverified claim rate in semantic test selection explanations.

metrics.name: Unsupported Claim Rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of LLM/RAG selection justifications that cite non-existent files, symbols, or fabricated call relationships.
metrics.formula: Unsupported_Claims / Total_Evaluated_Claims * 100 if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Extract all code symbols, file paths, and causal claims from RAG explanation outputs. Validate each citation against the repository AST. Flag non-existent or uncallable references.
questions.formula: Unsupported_Claims / Total_Evaluated_Claims * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: AST-grounded evidence vs pure LLM free-text reasoning.
questions.aggregation: Total unsupported claims divided by total claims across evaluated runs.
questions.interpretation: Measures hallucination resistance; zero unsupported claims indicates perfect evidence grounding.
questions.limitations: Requires parsing free-text or structured rationale fields into testable assertion claims.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires evaluation runs with LLM-generated rationale strings enabled.

questions.category: Category C — Repository RAG and Evidence Retrieval
questions.question: What are the retrieval success, timeout, fallback activation, and recovery rates for code intelligence and vector services?
questions.objective: Measure operational reliability and fault tolerance of external retrieval providers under varied network and load conditions.

metrics.name: Retrieval Success Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of retrieval requests completing within timeout without errors.
metrics.formula: Successful_Requests / Total_Requests * 100 if Total > 0 else null

metrics.name: Fallback Activation Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of requests where external service failure triggered local AST fallback.
metrics.formula: Fallback_Invocations / Total_Requests * 100 if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Monitor Sourcegraph and ChromaDB request telemetry during benchmark executions. Record timeouts, HTTP 5xx errors, fallback transitions, and successful fallbacks.
questions.formula: Successful_Requests / Total_Requests * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Remote Sourcegraph vs Local ChromaDB vs Local AST Fallback.
questions.aggregation: Aggregate event counts across all benchmark runs.
questions.interpretation: High fallback activation demonstrates system resilience, preventing pipeline crashes when remote services fail.
questions.limitations: Telemetry depends on logging fidelity and timeout threshold settings.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires logged retrieval operations across multiple benchmark executions.

questions.category: Category D — Test Generation and Ground Truth
questions.question: What are the parse, collection, and execution success rates of candidate tests synthesized for untested repositories?
questions.objective: Measure syntactic, import, and execution viability of automatically generated test suites across repositories with zero initial tests.

metrics.name: Parse Success Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of generated test files that compile and parse into valid AST without syntax errors.
metrics.formula: Valid_AST_Tests / Total_Generated_Tests * 100 if Total > 0 else null

metrics.name: Execution Pass Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of syntactically valid generated tests that pass cleanly on unmodified repository code.
metrics.formula: Passing_Tests / Total_Syntactically_Valid_Tests * 100 if Valid > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Generate candidate tests using AutoBenchmarkGenerator for repositories lacking existing test suites. Execute pytest in subprocess isolation and parse individual test outcomes.
questions.formula: Passing_Tests / Total_Generated_Tests * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: AutoBenchmarkGenerator template generation vs AST-driven signature inference.
questions.aggregation: Micro sum of test counts across all onboarded repositories.
questions.interpretation: High execution pass rate on unmodified code confirms generated tests are non-flaky baseline candidates.
questions.limitations: Passing on unmodified code does not prove test meaningfulness or fault sensitivity.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires candidate test generation runs on at least one registered repository.

questions.category: Category D — Test Generation and Ground Truth
questions.question: What is the mutation detection rate (mutant kill rate) of test suites against valid, non-equivalent controlled mutations?
questions.objective: Quantify fault-detection capability independently from test-selection precision and recall.

metrics.name: Mutant Kill Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of valid, non-equivalent AST mutants detected (killed) by test suite execution.
metrics.formula: Killed_Mutants / Valid_Mutants * 100 if Valid_Mutants > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Apply controlled AST operator and comparison mutations using AutoBenchmarkGenerator.cross_check_mutation_sensitivity. Execute candidate tests against each mutant. Record kills, survivals, and crashes.
questions.formula: Killed_Mutants / Valid_Mutants * 100 if Valid_Mutants > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Mutant kill rate of full suite vs TestPilot selected subset vs generated candidate tests.
questions.aggregation: Micro sum: total killed mutants / total valid mutants * 100 across repositories.
questions.interpretation: Directly measures test assertion quality and bug-catching power. Distinguishes trivial tests from rigorous tests.
questions.limitations: Equivalent mutants (syntactically changed but semantically identical) can artificially suppress kill rates if not filtered.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires execution of cross_check_mutation_sensitivity with at least 5 generated mutants.

questions.category: Category D — Test Generation and Ground Truth
questions.question: What is the historical bug reproduction rate across isolated Git worktrees of buggy and corrected revisions?
questions.objective: Determine the reliability of Method A ground truth validation in reproducing historical regressions before fix commits.

metrics.name: Bug Reproduction Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of historical bug cases where the regression test cleanly fails on buggy revision and passes on corrected revision.
metrics.formula: Reproduced_Bugs / Attempted_Bug_Cases * 100 if Attempted > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Create isolated Git worktrees for buggy and corrected commit SHAs. Execute regression test in subprocess isolation. Confirm failure on buggy commit and pass on corrected commit without environment crashes.
questions.formula: Reproduced_Bugs / Attempted_Bug_Cases * 100 if Attempted > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Historical bug validation success rate across commit distances (1 commit vs multi-commit fix).
questions.aggregation: Total reproduced cases divided by total submitted historical bug cases.
questions.interpretation: Validates Method A ground truth rigor: only bugs with reproducible before/after test evidence qualify as ground truth.
questions.limitations: Historical revisions may suffer from obsolete dependencies or incompatible runtime environments.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires registration of at least one historical bug fix case with valid commit SHAs.

questions.category: Category D — Test Generation and Ground Truth
questions.question: What are the distribution rates of benchmark cases across ground-truth review statuses?
questions.objective: Monitor ground-truth pipeline health and human review throughput across registered repositories.

metrics.name: Validation Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of benchmark cases in VALIDATED status.
metrics.formula: Validated_Cases / Total_Cases * 100 if Total > 0 else null

metrics.name: Stale Invalidation Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of benchmark cases marked STALE due to Git HEAD advancement.
metrics.formula: Stale_Cases / Total_Cases * 100 if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Query custom repository benchmark storage. Count cases across all 7 statuses: Candidate, Evidence Collection, Under Validation, Needs Human Review, Validated, Rejected, Stale.
questions.formula: Validated_Cases / Total_Cases * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Distribution breakdown across candidate, under-review, validated, rejected, and stale.
questions.aggregation: Status percentage breakdown across all registered repositories.
questions.interpretation: High validation rate indicates a mature benchmark suite; high stale rate indicates need to re-validate against updated HEAD revisions.
questions.limitations: Review throughput depends on human auditor availability.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires at least one registered repository with benchmark cases.

questions.category: Category E — Performance and Scalability
questions.question: What is the end-to-end execution time and time savings across all four evaluation configurations?
questions.objective: Quantify developer and CI pipeline time savings enabled by change-aware test selection compared to full regression runs.

metrics.name: CI Time Savings
metrics.definition: Execution time of full test suite minus (selection latency + execution time of selected tests).
metrics.formula: Time_Full_Suite - (Time_Selection + Time_Selected_Tests)

metrics.name: Speedup Factor
metrics.definition: Ratio of full regression time to selection pipeline plus selected test execution time.
metrics.formula: Time_Full_Regression / Total_Pipeline_Time if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Measure wall-clock time for Full Regression execution. For TestPilot and Naive, sum selection latency and selected test execution duration.
questions.formula: Time_Full_Suite - (Time_Selection + Time_Selected_Tests)
questions.comparison: Full Regression vs Naive Baseline vs TestPilot vs TestPilot + Repository RAG.
questions.aggregation: Total cumulative time saved across all evaluated commits.
questions.interpretation: Demonstrates net practical developer productivity gains, accounting for selection overhead.
questions.limitations: In fast test suites (< 5 seconds), selection overhead can exceed test execution time.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires recorded test execution runtimes in addition to selection algorithm latencies.

questions.category: Category E — Performance and Scalability
questions.question: What is the time overhead attributable to inspection, AST analysis, semantic analysis, RAG retrieval, selection, and other pipeline stages?
questions.objective: Profile pipeline latency hotspots to identify optimization targets across AST parsing, vector search, and model inference.

metrics.name: Stage Latency Breakdown
metrics.definition: Duration and percentage of total pipeline time consumed by each discrete analysis stage.
metrics.formula: Stage_Latency_ms / Total_Pipeline_Latency_ms * 100 if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Record high-resolution performance counters (time.perf_counter) before and after diff analysis, AST parsing, RAG retrieval, and test selection.
questions.formula: Stage_Latency_ms / Total_Pipeline_Latency_ms * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Latency contribution of each stage across repository sizes.
questions.aggregation: Average stage breakdown percentages across benchmark runs.
questions.interpretation: Identifies architectural bottlenecks (e.g. whether AST parsing or embedding search dominates runtime).
questions.limitations: Sub-millisecond stages on small repositories are sensitive to operating system scheduling noise.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires EvaluationRun objects with populated latency_ms fields.

questions.category: Category E — Performance and Scalability
questions.question: How do runtime, memory usage, and completion rate scale as repository size and test/dependency counts increase?
questions.objective: Evaluate computational complexity and resource scalability across codebases from hundreds to tens of thousands of files.

metrics.name: Latency Scaling Rate
metrics.definition: Growth in selection latency relative to lines of code or total test count.
metrics.formula: null

metrics.name: Completion Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of benchmark runs completing successfully without out-of-memory or timeout errors.
metrics.formula: Completed_Runs / Total_Initiated_Runs * 100 if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Benchmark TestPilot across repositories spanning small (< 1k LOC), medium (10k-50k LOC), and large (> 100k LOC) codebases (e.g. Flask, Django, Home Assistant). Plot latency vs LOC.
questions.formula: null
questions.comparison: Scaling curves of AST selection vs Naive Baseline vs Vector RAG.
questions.aggregation: Linear and log-log regression fit across repository scale tiers.
questions.interpretation: Sub-linear or linear scaling confirms viability for enterprise-scale monorepos.
questions.limitations: Memory profiling requires OS-specific process telemetry across platforms.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires benchmark executions across at least 3 repositories of differing scale tiers.

questions.category: Category F — Reliability and Generalization
questions.question: What is the consistency of selections and metrics across repeated runs with identical inputs and settings?
questions.objective: Verify deterministic reproducibility of test selection algorithms and benchmark evaluation pipelines.

metrics.name: Selection Jaccard Consistency
metrics.definition: Jaccard similarity coefficient between selected test sets across repeated executions on identical commits.
metrics.formula: |Selection_A ∩ Selection_B| / |Selection_A ∪ Selection_B| if Union > 0 else 1.0

questions.methodology: Execute the evaluation pipeline 5 consecutive times on identical commits and settings. Compute pairwise Jaccard similarity across selected test sets.
questions.formula: |Selection_A ∩ Selection_B| / |Selection_A ∪ Selection_B| if Union > 0 else 1.0
questions.comparison: Deterministic TestPilot (expected Jaccard = 1.0) vs LLM/RAG selection (temperature > 0).
questions.aggregation: Mean pairwise Jaccard consistency across all repeated trial pairs.
questions.interpretation: A Jaccard score of 1.0 proves 100% deterministic reproducibility, essential for CI confidence.
questions.limitations: Non-deterministic LLM temperatures can cause selection jitter if temperature is not pinned to 0.0.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires at least 2 independent evaluation runs on identical input commits.

questions.category: Category F — Reliability and Generalization
questions.question: What is the performance variation across independently evaluated repositories?
questions.objective: Assess cross-repository generalization and determine whether selection quality remains consistent across disparate architectures.

metrics.name: Precision Cross-Repo Standard Deviation
metrics.definition: Standard deviation of macro precision rates across evaluated repositories.
metrics.formula: sqrt(sum((Precision_i - Mean_Precision)^2) / (N - 1)) if N > 1 else null

metrics.name: Recall Cross-Repo Standard Deviation
metrics.definition: Standard deviation of macro recall rates across evaluated repositories.
metrics.formula: sqrt(sum((Recall_i - Mean_Recall)^2) / (N - 1)) if N > 1 else null

questions.methodology: Calculate macro precision, recall, and reduction for each evaluated repository. Compute standard deviation, interquartile range, and min-max spread.
questions.formula: sqrt(sum((Precision_i - Mean_Precision)^2) / (N - 1)) if N > 1 else null
questions.comparison: Cross-repository variance of TestPilot vs Naive Baseline.
questions.aggregation: Sample standard deviation across distinct repository records.
questions.interpretation: Low standard deviation indicates robust generalization; high variance points to architectural dependencies.
questions.limitations: Requires a diverse sample of at least 3 distinct repositories to compute meaningful variance.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires evaluated benchmark runs across at least 3 distinct repositories.

questions.category: Category F — Reliability and Generalization
questions.question: How does test-selection accuracy vary across supported change types and languages/frameworks?
questions.objective: Identify architectural sensitivities and failure modes across syntactic change patterns and dynamic vs static language features.

metrics.name: Accuracy by Change Type
metrics.definition: Precision and recall stratified by modification type (function modification, class refactoring, signature change, deletion).
metrics.formula: null

questions.methodology: Tag each benchmark case by change type (e.g. signature modification vs body edit) and language (Python, TypeScript, Go). Group evaluation metrics by tag and compute subgroup averages.
questions.formula: null
questions.comparison: Change type stratification (Signature vs Body vs Import vs Deletion).
questions.aggregation: Subgroup means across change categories.
questions.interpretation: Reveals whether specific change categories (like class inheritance or dynamic kwargs) suffer systematic recall loss.
questions.limitations: Categorizing real-world multi-file commits into a single change type can oversimplify complex diffs.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires benchmark cases annotated with change_type and language metadata.

questions.category: Category G — Evaluation Validity and Usability
questions.question: What is the benchmark validity rate across ground-truth coverage, revision reproducibility, provenance completeness, and metric answerability?
questions.objective: Audit the scientific integrity of evaluation benchmarks to ensure no unvalidated, unpinned, or unanswerable benchmarks enter official reports.

metrics.name: Scientific Validity Score
metrics.definition: Percentage of benchmark cases satisfying all 4 validity criteria: verified ground truth, pinned Git SHA, documented provenance, and non-empty test universe.
metrics.formula: Fully_Valid_Cases / Total_Cases * 100 if Total > 0 else null

questions.methodology: Audit every BenchmarkCase in storage. Verify: (1) is_verified is true, (2) base/target commit SHAs resolve in Git, (3) provenance field is non-empty, (4) total eligible tests > 0.
questions.formula: Fully_Valid_Cases / Total_Cases * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Verified benchmark cases vs unverified candidate cases.
questions.aggregation: Proportion of valid cases across custom and authoritative benchmark stores.
questions.interpretation: Guarantees evaluation results are scientifically defensible and free from fabricated ground truth.
questions.limitations: Automated audit checks structure and flags; human review is required to verify provenance veracity.
questions.answerability_requirements: Audit can be performed immediately on any populated benchmark store.

questions.category: Category G — Evaluation Validity and Usability
questions.question: What is the successful evaluation completion rate and frequency of manual intervention due to missing tests, unsupported environments, invalid ground truth, or execution failures?
questions.objective: Measure end-to-end automation reliability and developer friction when evaluating newly onboarded repositories.

metrics.name: Automated Completion Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of onboarded repositories that complete inspection, benchmark generation, and baseline evaluation without manual intervention.
metrics.formula: Completed_Without_Intervention / Total_Onboarded_Repos * 100 if Total > 0 else null

metrics.name: Intervention Frequency by Cause
metrics.definition: Categorized distribution of manual interventions (missing tests, environment crashes, unsupported language, invalid ground truth).
metrics.formula: null

questions.methodology: Track onboarding and evaluation runs in CustomRepositoryBenchmarkManager. Log error events, excluded repository reasons, and human review requests.
questions.formula: Completed_Without_Intervention / Total_Onboarded_Repos * 100 if Total > 0 else null
questions.comparison: Zero-configuration automated repositories vs repositories requiring manual test setup.
questions.aggregation: Aggregate success percentage and failure reason counts across all registered repos.
questions.interpretation: Identifies real-world onboarding friction points and directs test framework compatibility improvements.
questions.limitations: Environmental issues (e.g. missing virtualenv dependencies) reflect user environment rather than core algorithm defects.
questions.answerability_requirements: Requires tracking records for at least 3 repository onboarding attempts.
